events.title: NestJS introduced
events.summary: Kamil Myśliwiec started NestJS — a [TypeScript]-first [Node.js] framework inspired by Angular's module/DI architecture.
events.about: NestJS structures [Node.js] backends like Spring or Angular — modules, controllers, dependency injection, decorators. Used for [REST] and GraphQL APIs, [microservices], and enterprise [TypeScript] servers. Example: a typed [API] with auth guards, Swagger docs, and PostgreSQL via TypeORM — without Express spaghetti.

narrative.whyChosen: NestJS brought structure to [Node] backends when Express-only codebases became hard to maintain at scale.
narrative.whyImportant: Decorators, dependency injection, and modules made enterprise patterns normal in [TypeScript] APIs.
narrative.problemSolved: [Node.js] lacked a batteries-included, opinionated framework comparable to Spring or Angular.

events.title: WebAssembly MVP design finished
events.summary: Browser vendors reached [WebAssembly] MVP design consensus on February 28, 2017 — portable binary code for browsers; [Firefox] 52 began shipping Wasm in early March 2017.
events.about: [WebAssembly] (Wasm) runs C, C++, [Rust], and other languages in the browser at near-native speed — games, video editors, and Figma-class apps in the tab. Also runs on servers (Wasmtime, Wasmer) and as a portable sandbox. Compiles from [LLVM] and ships as a compact `.wasm` binary.

narrative.whyChosen: [WebAssembly] became the fourth web platform language alongside [HTML], [CSS], and JavaScript.
narrative.whyImportant: It let existing native codebases run in browsers without rewriting everything in JS.
narrative.problemSolved: JavaScript could not match native performance for heavy compute; asm.js proved the concept but needed a standard binary format.
